AnvilHDL
Timing-safe Hardware Description Language
Documentation Playground Preprint Zulip

AnvilHDL is a timing-safe hardware description language that combines clear, concise syntax with explicit timing semantics to produce predictable, verifiable, and synthesizable digital designs.

Why AnvilHDL

AnvilHDL is a timing-safe hardware description language designed for predictable, verifiable digital design. Key features include:

  • Timing-safe semantics — explicit, deterministic timing model prevents inadvertent race conditions and makes behavior predictable across synthesis and simulation.
  • Cycle-accurate simulation — supports fast, reproducible simulations that match the specified timing semantics.
  • Synthesizable constructs — high-level abstractions that map cleanly to RTL while preserving timing constraints.
  • Modular composition — hierarchical modules and clear interfaces enable reusable, testable blocks.
  • Concurrency primitives — built-in constructs for safe concurrent behavior without hidden timing hazards.
  • Formal-verification friendly — language design encourages properties that are easier to prove and check with formal tools.
  • Clear, concise syntax — minimal boilerplate for common patterns, improving readability and maintainability.
  • Toolchain integration — designed to integrate with common simulators, synthesis flows, and CI/testbench ecosystems.

Together these features make AnvilHDL well-suited for developing reliable, high-performance hardware with predictable timing and strong verification support.
